answer: A social-graph vouching thread ties every newcomer to three established sponsors, each staking 500 POA that is slashed if the newcomer is proven fake. Sponsors may vouch for at most two newcomers per epoch, so a fake army needs a wide, costly web of real backers. Each vouch is stamped like a jade seal on the ledger, unique and revocable only by its sponsor. An agent's voyage through the economy then rides on its sponsors' reputation: one proven fake burns all three stakes and flags the sponsors for review, making mass forgery far costlier than honest entry.
